assembly_notes:
Frame: +X is the front (card slot / command key end), +Z is up, +Y is the user's right (the magstripe side), adopted from the silver hero. The terminal housing is always one part; it is the root under flat_feet and the child of a support root otherwise.

Every top-face component is placed by querying the housing's real top surface at its station -- _face_z(x) and _face_pitch(x) -- never by a constant carried over from one source. That is what lets the two housing builds and the two entry faces combine without a gate: extruded_wedge derives a flat entry deck exactly as long as the active entry face needs (long under numeric_keypad, a narrow front lip under touchscreen_glass) while intersected_wedge presents one continuous plane, and the same key/display/strip placement code lands correctly on either.

The two remaining cross-slot conflicts are resolved by derivation, not exclusion: touchscreen_glass retreats its front edge behind the soft-key strip when that aux row is active, and side_hard_buttons are stationed below the magstripe groove floor the card interface cut into the right side.

Joint mating: every revolute and continuous joint is solved with mate_axes from a real provider/consumer AxisInterface pair and registered with register_interface_mate -- the cover hinge line at the rear rim, the roll spindle in the bay side-wall bearings, the display hinge at the top-rear slope edge, the cradle recline pivot on the tray surface, and the pedestal yaw axis through the collar. Prismatic key presses and the card slide run along real face normals with their apertures declared as surface_relations.

The magstripe groove is a boolean cut in the housing whose length derives from housing_length_m, and its dark liner derives from that cut length, so no liner can extend past the case.

derived.expression: 0.0 if housing_build == 'intersected_wedge' else housing_length_m * (0.50 if input_face == 'numeric_keypad' else 0.14)
derived.name: deck_len_m
derived.rationale: the extruded shell derives a flat entry deck exactly as long as the active entry face needs, so the keypad block lands on a flat plane and the glass slab gets one dominant sloped plane; the intersected shell needs no deck

derived.expression: the display station is re-solved on whichever face plane the housing actually presents at that station
derived.name: display_center_x_m
derived.rationale: every face-mounted visual is placed by querying the real top surface, never by a constant carried over from one housing

derived.name: glass_front_x_m
derived.rationale: the screen and the physical soft keys each take their own share of the face: the glass keeps the upper part, the strip sits low in the apron below it, and the guard term keeps them from overlapping. This is how the screen-dominant face and a physical key row combine without a gate

derived.name: aux_row_z_m
derived.rationale: the side button row is placed below the magstripe groove floor the card interface cut, so the two right-side features never intersect

derived.name: cover_len_m
derived.rationale: the cover is sized from the bay opening the housing cut, so it spans the bay and lands on the front rim at every case length

derived.name: bay_floor_z_m
derived.rationale: the bay floor follows the rear deck height so the roll and the cover keep their clearance when the wedge moves

derived.name: card_len_m
derived.rationale: the card derives from the pocket the housing cut plus its own travel, so it is retained by at least 8 mm at full withdrawal

derived.name: card_width_m
derived.rationale: the card derives from the pocket width with a running clearance

derived.name: head_local_seat_m
derived.rationale: the head's local bezel and screen offsets are the face station minus the hinge origin, so the closed head lies exactly in the face plane for both housings and both entry faces

derived.name: bracket_len_m
derived.rationale: the housing bracket is derived from the boss it cradles

derived.name: mount_height_m
derived.rationale: the housing is lifted to whichever seat the active support root presents, and the feet move onto that root

derived.expression: 0.0 (the housing origin, on the mate axis)
derived.name: mount_pivot_x_m
derived.rationale: a revolute rotates about its child-frame origin, so the mount axis passes through the terminal's own origin for both roots: the cradle derives a recline well for the tail that then swings below the tray, and the pedestal collar sits directly under it

multiplicities.host_capacity_expression: 2 <= aux_key_count <= 6. The soft key strip is the host and widens with N (aux_strip_width_m = N * aux_key_size_m + (N + 1) * 0.0035), exactly as the N=6 source widened the strip from 0.064 m to 0.076 m; the narrowest 0.070 m case still fits six 0.0045 m caps. The side row's usable run is 0.34 * housing_length_m below the magstripe groove, which holds six caps on the shortest 0.150 m case.
multiplicities.name: aux_key_count
multiplicities.spacing_expression: the N caps are evenly spaced and symmetric about their host centre: on the soft key strip they span Y with pitch aux_span_m / (N - 1) where aux_span_m = aux_strip_len_m - aux_key_size_m; on the side row they span X with the same rule over the usable side run. Cap size derives from the pitch so neighbours keep a gap at N=6.

candidates.evidence: Six-point side profile extruded across the full width and filleted on the vertical edges, giving a two-stage silhouette: a vertical front-face band, a flat keypad deck, a short display slope, then a flat rear deck. The printer cavity, chip pocket and side magstripe groove are boolean cuts out of that solid, and the slope's unit normal and pitch are computed from the same profile points that built it.

candidates.name: extruded_wedge
candidates.notes: Six-point polyline in the XZ plane extruded across the full width and filleted on the vertical edges, then detailed with boolean cuts. Keeps the vertical front-face band, the flat entry deck and the flat rear deck, so the silhouette stays two-stage even when the entry face shrinks the deck.

candidates.evidence: A charcoal keypad plate proud of the sloped face with a framed LCD above it, and a field of lofted keycaps in three sizes seated into the plate: four function keys, a 3x4 numeric block, and a wide red/yellow/green command row, each an independent prismatic press along the face normal. Corroborated by the silver hero's equivalent 12-key grid plus command triad at model.py:L299-L338.

surface_relation.motion_expression: pressing q in [0, key_travel_m] moves the cap -q along the face normal; at q = key_travel_m the cap still protrudes keycap_height_m - key_travel_m >= 0.0022 m
surface_relation.normal_band_expression: cap base sits at -0.0002 m (seated into the plate) and the crown reaches +keycap_height_m along the local face normal
surface_relation.opening_expression: each key owns a keycap_x_m by keycap_y_m aperture in the keypad plate centred on its row/column station; the whole 4-row block plus the command row stays inside keypad_plate_len_m by keypad_plate_width_m
surface_relation.required_author_check: category_anchor: every entry key stays inside its deck aperture and keeps its exposed band

candidates.name: numeric_keypad
candidates.notes: Charcoal keypad plate proud of the top face carrying a 3x4 numeric block and a wide red/amber/green command row, plus a framed LCD above it. Fifteen independent prismatic presses along the local face normal.

parameters.name: key_travel_m
parameters.rationale: prismatic press travel shared by the entry keys and the auxiliary key row; also sets the minimum keycap height so a pressed cap still stands proud

parameters.expression: slope_rear_x_m + 0.42 * (slope_front_x_m - slope_rear_x_m) if input_face == 'numeric_keypad' else (glass_front_x_m + glass_rear_x_m) / 2
parameters.name: display_center_x_m
parameters.rationale: station of the display on the top face; the small framed LCD sits on the slope, the glass slab is centred on whatever face length the aux row leaves free

parameters.name: display_len_m
parameters.rationale: display length along the face; a framed window on the keypad face, the whole free face length on the touchscreen face

parameters.expression: clamp(0.73 * body_width_m, 0.030, 0.072) if input_face == 'numeric_keypad' else clamp(0.83 * body_width_m, 0.040, 0.082)
parameters.name: display_width_m
parameters.rationale: display width across Y, always inside the face margin

parameters.expression: (cmd_row_x_m - entry_row0_x_m) / 4.75, with cmd_row_x_m anchored at the front edge and entry_row0_x_m pushed back behind the auxiliary strip
parameters.name: key_pitch_x_m
parameters.rationale: the key block is anchored at the front edge and its row pitch is derived from whatever run the auxiliary strip leaves. When a tilting display head needs more room than a short case has, the strip moves forward and the keypad compresses (key_size_x_m follows the pitch) instead of the display collapsing to a window too small to visibly tilt

parameters.name: key_pitch_y_m
parameters.rationale: column pitch of the numeric block and the command triad across the case width

parameters.name: keycap_height_m
parameters.rationale: keycap height is derived from travel so a fully pressed cap still stands 2.4 mm proud. The keypad plate is a perforated solid: each key runs in a real aperture cut through the plate and into the deck, so no cap ever penetrates its host

candidates.evidence: The same sloped face populated as a screen-dominant slab instead: one full-face dark bezel, a dark glass panel framed inside it, a thin status-bar strip, a camera lens standing on the face normal, and an NFC mark embedded in the front face. The keypad plate and the entire key field are gone, so the part tree loses the whole keypad sub-tree.
candidates.name: touchscreen_glass
candidates.notes: The same top face populated as a screen-dominant slab: a full-face bezel, a dark glass panel framed inside it, a status strip and a camera lens, plus an NFC mark on the front face. No numeric block and no keypad plate.

parameters.expression: slope_rear_x_m + 0.42 * (slope_front_x_m - slope_rear_x_m) if input_face == 'numeric_keypad' else (glass_front_x_m + glass_rear_x_m) / 2

parameters.name: glass_front_x_m
parameters.rationale: the glass keeps the upper 58% of the usable face and is independent of the auxiliary row, so moving the soft keys down the face opens a real gap under the screen instead of dragging the screen down with them. The second term is the guard that keeps screen and keys from ever overlapping

parameters.name: glass_rear_x_m
parameters.rationale: rear end of the glass, held clear of the paper exit slit and the bay rim, and of the tilting head's hinge station when that display mount is active

candidates.evidence: A dark strip on the deck just below the display carrying N identical keycaps, evenly spaced across its width, each an independent prismatic press downward into the strip top. The strip is the host: its width and the key spacing come from the same key-count list.

surface_relation.opening_expression: each cap owns an aux_key_size_m square opening in the strip centred on its even station; all N openings stay inside aux_strip_width_m

candidates.name: soft_key_strip

parameters.name: aux_key_size_m
parameters.rationale: key size shrinks with the pitch so six keys still leave a gap between neighbours

parameters.name: aux_cap_height_m
parameters.rationale: auxiliary cap height derived from travel so a pressed cap still stands 1.8 mm proud

parameters.name: aux_strip_width_m
parameters.rationale: the dark strip is the host and widens with the key count exactly as the N=6 source widened it from 0.064 m to 0.076 m; once it reaches the case width the caps shrink instead. The strip is a perforated solid seated 0.3 mm into the shell, so each cap runs in a real opening

parameters.expression: numeric_keypad: 0.035 * housing_length_m (pushed forward when a tilting head needs room). touchscreen_glass: glass_face_front_x_m + 0.42 * (face_front_x_m - glass_face_front_x_m), clamped to keep the strip clear of both the glass and the front boundary
parameters.name: aux_row_x_m
parameters.rationale: station of the strip on the top face. Under a keypad face it sits just below the display with the numeric block filling the face beneath it. Under a screen-dominant face there is no numeric block, so the strip is stationed low in the apron the glass leaves — around 57-70% down the usable face — and reads as a bottom control row rather than a rim tucked under the screen

parameters.name: knuckle_span_m
parameters.rationale: the two knuckle barrels and the housing bosses that flank them are spaced from the bay width, so the hinge hardware follows the case

parameters.name: exit_slit_x_m
parameters.rationale: paper exit slit station just in front of the cover front edge

candidates.evidence: Both card paths are openings in the shell with nothing inserted: a chip pocket cut into the front face backed by a dark liner at the slot's back wall, and a magstripe groove cut along the right side with a dark liner along its floor. The liner lengths are tied to the cut lengths, so the groove reads as a recess rather than an applied strip.
candidates.name: static_chip_slot
candidates.notes: Both card paths are openings with nothing inserted: a chip pocket cut into the front face backed by a liner at its back wall, and a magstripe groove cut along the right side with a liner along its floor. Both liner lengths derive from their cut lengths.

parameters.name: chip_slot_depth_m
parameters.rationale: how deep the chip pocket is cut into the front face. It is derived from the case length and from the stroke it has to retain a card through, so a fully withdrawn card is still held by at least 8 mm at every travel setting

parameters.name: chip_slot_width_m
parameters.rationale: chip pocket width, inside the case side walls

parameters.name: groove_floor_z_m
parameters.rationale: magstripe groove floor height on the right side, derived from the front-edge height so the groove stays inside the wall at every wedge setting

parameters.name: groove_liner_len_m
parameters.rationale: the dark liner is derived from the cut length it lines, so it can never extend beyond the housing it belongs to

candidates.evidence: The chip slot is occupied: a filleted card plate with a logo patch and a stripe band is a separate part resting on the slot floor and protruding past the front face, on a prismatic slide that withdraws it toward the user while keeping part of it retained in the slot. Adds a part and a joint the static reading does not have.
candidates.name: sliding_bank_card
candidates.notes: The chip slot is occupied: a filleted card plate with a logo patch and a stripe band on a prismatic slide that withdraws it toward the user while keeping it retained.

parameters.name: card_travel_m
parameters.rationale: withdraw travel of the inserted chip card; the card must stay retained in the slot at full travel

parameters.name: chip_slot_depth_m
parameters.rationale: how deep the chip pocket is cut into the front face. It is derived from the case length and from the stroke it has to retain a card through, so a fully withdrawn card is still held by at least 8 mm at every travel setting

parameters.name: chip_slot_width_m
parameters.rationale: chip pocket width, inside the case side walls

parameters.name: groove_floor_z_m
parameters.rationale: magstripe groove floor height on the right side, derived from the front-edge height so the groove stays inside the wall at every wedge setting

parameters.name: groove_liner_len_m
parameters.rationale: the dark liner is derived from the cut length it lines, so it can never extend beyond the housing it belongs to

parameters.name: card_len_m
parameters.rationale: the card is sized from the slot it lives in plus the travel it must survive, so it is still retained by at least 8 mm when fully withdrawn

parameters.name: card_width_m
parameters.rationale: the card is derived from the slot width so it stays centred with a running clearance

candidates.evidence: The housing is itself the grounded root, standing on four rubber pads lightly embedded into its underside at the four corners. No support part and no mount joint.
candidates.name: flat_feet
candidates.notes: The housing is the grounded root, standing on four rubber pads at its corners.

parameters.name: foot_station_x_m
parameters.rationale: foot stations follow the case length so the four pads stay under the corners

parameters.name: foot_station_y_m
parameters.rationale: foot stations follow the case width

parameters.name: foot_radius_m
parameters.rationale: pad radius scaled with the case

candidates.evidence: A cradle tray with a rear upstand wall and a front locating lip becomes the grounded root; the feet migrate to its underside, gold charging pads sit on the tray top, and a revolute about -Y at the tray surface reclines the terminal against the upstand. The housing stops being the root and gains a parent.

dimensions.radius: recline pivot on the tray surface near the rear of the cradle

candidates.name: tilt_dock
candidates.notes: A cradle tray with a rear upstand and a front locating lip is the grounded root; the feet migrate to its underside, charging pads sit on the tray top, and a revolute about -Y at the tray surface reclines the terminal.

parameters.name: dock_recline_rad
parameters.rationale: upper limit of the cradle recline hinge; the terminal tail must stay clear of the tray while the front rises

parameters.name: cradle_len_m
parameters.rationale: the tray is derived from the terminal it holds, so the case always lands inside the upstand and the front lip

parameters.name: cradle_width_m
parameters.rationale: tray width derived from the terminal plus the two rear retention posts that stand outboard of it

parameters.name: cradle_height_m
parameters.rationale: tray thickness; also the height of the recline pivot above the counter

parameters.name: upstand_height_m
parameters.rationale: height of the two rear retention posts, derived from the terminal's rear height. They stand outboard of the case width rather than forming one solid wall, so the opened printer cover swings through the open centre even at full recline

parameters.name: post_width_m
parameters.rationale: the rear retention posts sit just outboard of the terminal, leaving a centre gap wider than cover_width_m so the reclined cover never meets them

parameters.expression: (housing_length_m / 2) * sin(dock_recline_rad) + 0.004, with cradle_height_m = max(clamp(0.205 * housing_length_m, 0.028, 0.046), well_depth_m + 0.009)
parameters.name: well_depth_m
parameters.rationale: the recline pivot sits at the terminal's own origin, so the tail swings below the tray surface; the tray derives a well deep enough for that swing and a height that still leaves a floor under it

candidates.evidence: A weighted disk base, a column and a bearing collar form the grounded root, with an annular chrome trim ring let into the base perimeter and the feet on its underside. The mount joint is a revolute about vertical Z at the collar top, so the terminal yaws at raised height instead of reclining on a tray — a different root profile and a different axis direction from the cradle.

dimensions.radius: vertical yaw axis through the collar centre, radius collar_radius_m

candidates.name: swivel_pedestal
candidates.notes: A weighted disk base, a column and a bearing collar form the grounded root with a trim ring at the perimeter and feet underneath; a revolute about vertical Z at the collar top yaws the terminal at raised height.

parameters.name: pedestal_yaw_rad
parameters.rationale: symmetric yaw limit of the pedestal swivel; the terminal must clear the column at both extremes

parameters.name: base_radius_m
parameters.rationale: the weighted disk is derived from the terminal it must counterbalance

parameters.name: pole_height_m
parameters.rationale: column height scaled with the terminal

parameters.name: collar_radius_m
parameters.rationale: the bearing collar is derived from the case width so the underside always lands on a real seat

parameters.name: stand_top_z_m
parameters.rationale: mount height of the swivel; the terminal underside sits on it
